programmes.d: Notepad points to kidnapper.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica. The police rely on cell phone mapping, wiretapping and a host of forensic evidence to link a suspect to a murder.
Shortly after daybreak in Vancouver, British Columbia, a fire was set in a dumpster.

In 1994, 19-year-old Shannon Melendi disappeared while at Emory University. Her disappearance remained a mystery for ten years, until new scientific testing cast a different light on Colvin "Butch" Hinton.
In 1991, San Francisco pornographer Artie Mitchell was murdered in his home.
Sometime during a neighborhood Christmas party, five-year-old Melissa Brannen disappeared. Investigators turned to forensic science to help them see what the witnesses missed.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body.

It was one of the most brazen crimes of the 20th century. Adolph Coors III, chairman of the Coors Brewing Company, was kidnapped and held for ransom. The crime prompted one of the most intense manhunts in United States history.
Authorities track a kidnapper who let his victim write a last will and informed the family of her murder. A phone number written on a previous page left a lasting impression, which helped to convict.
A woman, who had recently rejected a co-worker half her age, ends up dead in her driveway.
Dianna Green was brutally attacked in her own home and her unborn child was killed.
In 1986, Gary Dale Larson was stabbed to death in his Edmond, Oklahoma home. The killer then sexually assaulted Larson's girlfriend, Janet Haynes.
This episode documents a deadly bombing at a church in Oakwood, Illinois, in December 1997.
Lives changed in the 20 years following an unsolved murder, and so did forensic science. In time, a high-powered microscope and DNA profiling revealed a clue no one had seen before.
Three fingerprints on a window screen are enough for a print examiner to uncover a serial killer.
An infant is rushed to the emergency room with serious breathing problems. Within months, there are more than 30 similar cases. Can doctors find the cause and a cure?
All evidence leads to the wife when a real estate developer is murdered.

No one in a quiet residential community saw anything unusual the day one of their neighbors was brutally attacked and murdered. Fingerprints found at the crime scene and surveillance video helped investigators to apprehend the presumed killer.
The woman had been sexually assaulted, stabbed repeatedly, and left for dead.

When police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife, authorities linked 20 cat hairs found on her jacket to a cat owned by Beamish's parents. It was the first time animal DNA was used to solve a criminal case.
Women in a Louisiana city live in fear of a rapist who leaves no clues to his identity.

Digital enhancement of security camera footage shows that what appears to be a casual encounter is actually a forced abduction. When investigators suspect the crimes are not random, they fear a serial killer may be on the loose.
Debate over cause of death.

When a fire destroyed most of a home and a young boy went missing, police organized the largest search in the history of their small town. First the boy's backpack was discovered five miles from home, then his body was found 50 miles away.
A mother and her two young daughters are found brutally murdered and sexually violated.
A serial rapist is on the loose in a Texas town. No one knew where he'd strike next, but the audacity of his attacks and the escalation of violence against his victims made finding him imperative.
The sensitive nose of a forensic examiner sniffs out murder.

The body of a young girl was discovered on isolated farmland near Delano, California. She had no ID, but police found mailbox keys in the pocket of her jeans. With no other clues, they checked the mailboxes of every apartment building in Delano.
In rural Canada, a doctor is accused of sedating and sexually assaulting a female patient.
In 1962, the small town residents of Hanford, California lost their sense of peace when one of their own, 15-year-old Marlene Miller, was murdered.
Clues at the scene of a possible murder-suicide lead investigators to believe otherwise.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun. Scientists use unique methods to lift the serial number from the weapon to trace it to its owner
A forensic scientist uses his skills to preserve a footprint left in snow.

When convenience store employee Wanda Mason is found dead, investigators find the entire murder has been caught on the store's security camera. But the image of the killer is so degraded it seems impossible to positively identify him.
Tracey Frame, 35, was convicted of killing David Nixon after he planned to end their relationship.
Doctors don't know why a young scientist has fallen gravely ill. When tests finally reveal the cause, it's too late to save him.
Forensics determines whether a woman's death in a fire is due to arson, murder or accident.
In 1991, Grand Junction, Colorado is on edge after a series of deadly bombings kill two people and injure one more. Police race to find the culprit before he strikes again.
A woman is found dead from a gunshot wound and police suspect her husband.

In 1996, a federal agency ruled that Terri Strickland had intentionally set the fire that killed her 17-month-old son, Josh Hinson. Using the then-emerging resources of the internet, Strickland undertook her own investigation.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.
In 2004, nursing student Tamika Huston went missing from her Spartanburg, South Carolina home. A tip led detectives to her car, where they found an unknown house key that could help solve the case.
Fire wood found at a crime scene helps investigators locate a killer.

The doctors at the hospital couldn't determine the cause of Bobby Curley's hallucinations and intense pain. They treated it as a neurological disorder but his condition deteriorated. He was being poisoned.
Police collect evidence leading to a driver who fatally injured a cyclist in a hit-and-run accident.
When a woman and her daughter didn't return home from shopping, her husband directed police to a nearby mall. The child's body was found, but there was no sign of the wife.
On May 12, 1994, Crystal Perry was viciously murdered in her home in Bridgton, Maine.

In 1993, the state of Florida was known for more than just Disney World. Worldwide attention focused on a rash of robberies which targeted tourists. Some vacationers were killed in these attacks, but some fought and survived.
New clues are found in the form of a phone and shoes in a rape and murder case unsolved for 8 years.

When two women from the same town were murdered in the same way, police feared a serial killer was on the loose. At first they thought the victims had nothing in common until they found tiny clues linking them to the same man.
Four young adults are murdered in an affluent Texas neighborhood, with little evidence.
When a woman and her baby are found dead in a corn field, the obvious suspect is her husband.

The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage. Conventional means of identifying the victim are impossible, leading investigators to rely on DNA, forensic anthropology and toxicology.
A suspicious fire swept through an apartment killing two young women.

When a college student is reported missing, police believe their investigation will be like countless others. But when they discover blood spatter in her boyfriend's bedroom, they know this case is going to be different.
There was no clear reason for a young, healthy college student to be dead.

Robert Sims returns home after working the night shift and finds his wife unconscious on the kitchen floor. Their son is fast asleep in an upstairs bedroom, but their six-week-old daughter, Heather, is missing.
After 10 bodies turn up in Florida, one victim — 17-year-old Lisa McVey — is abducted but released. She leads police to the perpertrator, Bobbie Joe Long.
A man states that a robber shot his wife, but a song he downloaded makes investigators suspicious.
On May 20, 2001, Carrie Nelson, then 20, was beaten to death while working alone in a park office.

In 1996, more than a dozen children in Seattle, Washington, were fighting for their lives. Each one of them had contracted a serious unknown illness. After one died, investigators knew the clock was ticking.
When the decomposed body of a teenage girl is discovered, police have no clues to her identity.

Police instituted an intense search when the mother of two young children went missing. Twenty years after her body was found, new technology recontextualized old evidence and pointed directly to the killer.
When two women were found brutally murdered, police wondered if they were victims of a hate crime.
The victim was a self-made man who never minced words. Perhaps he was murdered by a disgruntled client or employee. Perhaps the racy photos in his safe held the clue to solving the crime.
Women in a Louisiana city live in fear of a rapist who leaves no clues to his identity.

An investigation into the murder of a World War II veteran slowed to a halt when the prime suspect had a solid alibi. But a lucky break led to a shady character who wore distinctive boots and had a sweet tooth.
Forensics contradicts a husband's confession to his wife's murder.

A man tells police he shot an intruder who had attacked and murdered his wife. The husband paints a tragic picture and is dubbed a hero. Four years later, forensic evidence leads police to re-examine the motives of this so-called hero.
Serial arsonist leaves no evidence.

Avis Banks and her unborn child were brutally murdered. The body was discovered by her fiancé, Keyon Pittman. When police learned that Pittman was having affairs with other women, he became the prime suspect.
Three fingerprints on a window screen are enough for a print examiner to uncover a serial killer.

In 2002, funeral director Lonnie Turner, Sr. was found shot to death. His son Lonnie Jr. became the prime suspect, particularly after it was discovered that the murder was committed with his gun. However, he had an alibi for the time of the murder.
Tests reveal the race, eye color and hair color of the person who killed two young women.

A bomb, constructed to cause as much damage as possible, kills a victim with deadly force and flame. When a painstaking search yields some tiny clues, police are able to identify the killer as surely as if he'd signed them.
A woman's death is ruled a suicide, but forensics later prove her husband is a key suspect.

When Genell Plude is found dead in her bathroom, the scene points to suicide. But a coroner's inquest and a unique application of forensic science give investigators a different explanation for her death.
Series premiere. A flight attendant went missing and was never seen again.

A woman is reported missing after a fight with her husband. Police suspect a man who reported a fire in his car. Two tiny drops of blood are found in the interior. Finally, a tiny clue inside the suspect's watchband helps solve the case.
A nosy neighbor with a disturbing obsession becomes a suspect in a woman's murder.
When police doubt a young girl's story about being abused, fibers on her clothes help her case.
A retired police officer is found dead with a single gunshot wound to the head. His wife says the motive was robbery, but later tells police he committed suicide.
Investigators solve the 1988 murder of a drifter by examining a species of fly found near the body.

When Joann Katrinak is found dead in a corn field with her infant son, the obvious suspect is the husband and father of the victims. But insects found on the bodies reveal a vital clue which uncovers a twisted story of passion gone wrong.
Investigators come to suspect a wife's bathtub drowning may not have been an accident.

A young TV news producer is raped and murdered in her apartment. Police identify two suspects, but both are cleared of any wrongdoing. When the case stalls for more than a year, investigators turn to the Commonwealth of Virginia's DNA Databank.
Two men die of heart disease six years apart and each was once married to the same woman.

When investigators found Bruce Miller dead in the office of his junkyard business, the crime scene was almost pristine. But when a computer forensics expert examined computers owned by the victim's wife and her lover, he found all the evidence needed.
A shoe impression leads investigators on the right track to finding a killer.

A young hairdresser was sexually assaulted and murdered in her own beauty salon. The evidence at the crime scene didn't match any of the suspects and, after the initial investigation, the case went cold for ten years.
A union official is executed in his home not long after a strike by the union membership.
Responding to a 2008 garage fire, Illinois emergency response discovered a man crushed beneath a truck.
When a young woman disappears, investigators discover that she led a double life.

When a policeman's house goes up in flames, experts suspect arson. The officer whose home was torched arrests low-level drug dealer James Wren, who confesses. But when the suspect vanishes, investigators question the authenticity of the confession.
After shooting his victims, the killer placed the evidence into a bag and tossed it into the river.
A lifelong resident of the tiny town of Lefroy, Tasmania was murdered outside his own home. Robbery appeared to be the motive, but with no suspects, the investigation came to a halt.
In 2002, funeral director Lonnie Turner, Sr. was found shot to death.

In this classic episode of Forensic Files, the longest-running true crime series in television history, Eileen and Derrick Severs disappear from their home in a small village in Great Britain and police find evidence of foul play.

A talented television news anchor is shot to death outside her home.
The victim had ingested a massive amount of cyanide. An unlikely clue — a flaw on a mailing envelope — exposed a murderer who was willing to kill innocent people.
A woman is haunted by the memory of her father murdering her mother.
